transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's medication-safety huddle. As you know, we introduced the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol this Monday for our adult inpatients, and before we allow it to be used on the upcoming night shift, I need to hear from each of you regarding any operational findings. Pharmacy, laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical information technology — please report anything you've observed so far. I'll be making the final decision on any temporary safety protocol and required safeguards this afternoon, so your input is critical right now.

transcript.text: I need to report a significant safety concern from pharmacy. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. To mitigate this risk, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and instead supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: From laboratory medicine, I need to report that our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this anticoagulant protocol is an aPTT test every six hours.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From nursing education, I need to report a critical staffing competency concern. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they are permitted to administer this medication.

This alert will warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before the order can be released, which directly addresses the selection errors pharmacy has already observed.

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on bedside automated dispensing cabinet stock of the anticoagulant; pharmacy-prepared syringes only until the medication safety review is complete and concentration selection safeguards are in place.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the temporary hold to eliminate selection errors between 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL concentrations.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: Use aPTT testing every six hours as the approved replacement for anti-Xa monitoring until the anti-Xa analyzer is available for calibration on Friday at 17:00.
decisions.nurse_authorization: Require charge-nurse sign-off before any of the 18 identified nurses who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module are permitted to administer this medication on tonight's shift.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today to warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before order release.

commitments.detail: Remove bedside stock from automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the temporary hold.
Confirm aPTT testing every six hours is operational for tonight's shift and notify nursing of the monitoring requirement.
Ensure charge-nurse sign-off is enforced for the 18 nurses who have not completed the competency module before they administer this anticoagulant.
Deploy the electronic medication-record concentration-selection alert at 16:00 today and confirm it is live before the night shift begins.
Reassess concentration selection error rates after the electronic alert and pharmacy-prepared syringe safeguards are in place before lifting the temporary hold.
